biography.html: Sergey Brin is a Moscow-born American computer scientist who co-founded Google with Larry Page. Trained in mathematics and computer science, he helped turn their Stanford research on ranking web pages by links into a search engine and technology company. He later directed substantial philanthropic support towards collaborative research on Parkinson’s disease and other neurological conditions.

confidence.reason: Official Google and Stanford sources support the education, PageRank and founding mechanism, while Forbes and the Michael J. Fox Foundation support the later neurological-research philanthropy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Mathematics and computer science gave Sergey Brin the tools for his defining project. He pursued graduate research at Stanford, where he met Larry Page. Together they developed PageRank, using links between web pages as a signal of relevance, and turned the research into Google.

Brin later stepped away from executive leadership while remaining a cofounder, shareholder and board member of Google’s parent company. His scientific interests also shaped a sustained philanthropic programme for neurological research. Through Aligning Science Across Parkinson’s, he has backed collaborative basic research, shared resources and open data intended to accelerate understanding of the disease.
